layers.note: An upright shrub of rocky slopes, canyons and washes.

moisture.note: Dry rocky slopes and sandy washes.

elevation_m.note: Up to about 1,520 m (Kearney and Peebles: up to 5,000 feet), mostly much lower.

coldest_c.note: Across its range, coldest-month means from about 7 to 22 °C; gone below 4 °C and above 25 °C.

hard_freeze_c.note: Across its range, lows to about −7 °C borne, gone where the year's coldest night falls below about −11 °C.

warmest_c.note: Across its range, warmest-month means from about 28 to 37 °C; gone below 25 °C, where summers are too short, and above 40 °C.

degree_days_0.note: About 5,800 to 12,500 degree-days above 0 °C, none below 4,500.

degree_days_5.note: About 4,000 to 10,500 degree-days above 5 °C, none below 3,000.

moisture_index.note: A moisture index from about 0.03, gone by 0.01.

summer_rain.note: No lower limit: it grows where winter rain falls alone (the Mojave and the low Colorado Desert) as well as where the July to September monsoon brings summer rain, as on the bajada (about half the year's); up to about 0.8 of the year's precipitation in summer, gone by 0.9.

provenance.notes: Authored for the Saguaro desert scene (the west bajada of Saguaro National Park's Tucson Mountain District, about 750 m) from general knowledge of the species, the ranges and elevations in Kearney and Peebles (1942) and, where one exists, the FEIS species review. Desert lavender grows in southern Arizona, southeastern California, southern Nevada and northwestern Mexico (Kearney and Peebles 1942; Abrams 1951), in the Sonoran and Colorado deserts. Each climate range brackets the climate of that range, an approximate envelope read from these descriptions, not fitted to occurrence records.
